dataset_version: football_matches (bulk open dataset), 7 seasons x 7 divisions
execution_assumptions: bets pre-match line, settles at that price; FrictionModel charges the same cost to the entry threshold and the P&L
hypothesis: A weighted-MLE Dixon-Coles fit produces a profitable 1X2 betting strategy on real football odds after friction.
notes: Motivated the CLV-baseline discipline (backtest/clv.py) and the thin-markets thesis tested next (673d7bc).

results.note: every division loses money; CLV vs a single book's close is negative except in the two thinnest markets tested (Scottish tiers, t=5.1 and t=4.1 vs the random-selection baseline), and even there the skill is worth less than the margin plus commission
results.sc3_significance: 0.5 standard errors from zero; noise, not an edge

search_method: single run, no hyperparameter search performed or logged
validation_interval: n/a -- single walk-forward pass, no separate validation split

dataset_version: football-data.co.uk, 22 divisions with closing odds, ~53,000 matches
execution_assumptions: odds-matched CLV baseline (not just uniform-random) to control for which prices the model favors
hypothesis: CLV skill increases with market thinness (proxied by mean single-book overround), pre-specified before viewing the out-of-sample result.
notes: Confirms genuine, statistically real selection skill in thin markets that still does not clear transaction costs -- the load-bearing null result behind this repo's 'capacity, not calibration' thesis.

parameters.test: Spearman correlation, thinness proxy vs CLV skill

results.confound_check: longshot-only pseudo-strategy scores large skill against uniform baseline, exactly zero against odds-matched baseline
results.mechanism_caveat: thin markets also have wider CLV dispersion (rho=0.661 with overround); normalizing keeps the point estimate but loses significance at n=15
results.significant_divisions: 14 of 15, t>2; English National League strongest at t=10.2
results.skill_magnitude_pct: 0.3 to 0.75 percentage points, vs a 5-9% overround

search_method: single pre-registered test (ONE Spearman correlation), no search
train_interval: 7 divisions used to form the hypothesis (not part of this test)

dataset_version: 20,503-event open snapshot; 38,993 resolved markets with realized outcomes; 863 with pre-resolution price history; 166 live order books
execution_assumptions: depth-walked executable sizing; cross-venue matches manually checked for resolution-criteria equivalence
hypothesis: At least one class of pure statistical arbitrage (negRisk, logical consistency, cross-venue vs Kalshi) is exploitable on Polymarket after fees.
notes: The headline finding that reframes the rest of this repo's Polymarket work: pure arbitrage is structurally capped by the quadratic fee near mid-price; any real edge has to come from forecasting, not price patterns.

results.apparent_longshot_underpricing_pts: 13-26, found to be a volume-tier selection artifact, not alpha
results.cross_venue_matched_question_rate: 14 of 30 sampled pairs were the same question

dataset_version: 794 full hourly price paths, strictly walk-forward
execution_assumptions: fee = 2.0c reference; spread/delay stress tests applied post-hoc to the one surviving horizon
hypothesis: Short-horizon price momentum or mean-reversion in Polymarket price series is tradeable after transaction costs.
notes: Closes the last untested pure-price stat-arb class with a clean negative result: the venue is not strong-form efficient (reversion is real) but the fee schedule is wider than the inefficiency.

results.mechanism: bid-ask bounce (alternating trades at bid/ask), not harvestable by a taker
results.momentum_correlation_range: -0.027 to -0.109, t from -3.5 to -8.9 (negative at every horizon)
results.significance_by_horizon: peaks at 24h, insignificant by 48h (t=1.63), gone by 72h

test_interval: 8 horizons, non-overlapping windows stepped by the forward horizon

hypothesis: Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift, measured with correct entry timing (first tradeable session, not announcement close), is present and monotone in SUE bucket.
notes: Sample is half mega-cap (data-access constrained by ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY availability), where PEAD should already be arbitraged away; repo notes it should be re-run on micro-caps with a key.

results.note: biggest misses drifted up, opposite of the prediction

dataset_version: real trailing earnings histories, 3 cached companies (IBM, HD, CULP) + Polymarket's live ~41 beat-earnings contracts
execution_assumptions: edge scored against bid/ask, not mid; ties count as misses per the contract's literal wording
hypothesis: A shrinkage-toward-base-rate model of trailing beat rate prices Polymarket's 'will X beat earnings' contracts better than the market, net of the correct bid/ask spread and the 'beat' (not meet-or-beat) resolution rule.
notes: Model carries genuine walk-forward information (Brier skill +0.09) but the one live market it can be tested against today produces no trade -- 'the market is approximately right', consistent with the calibration finding in 402eb97 that Polymarket is well-priced wherever liquid.

parameters.prior: shrinkage toward base rate of tickers with live Polymarket markets only (not all cached tickers)

results.note: correct large-cap-only prior produces -0.1c edge on the one live HD market (no trade); the wrong pooled-prior version had produced a false +3.5c BUY NO, caused by one micro-cap ticker with no live market contaminating the prior by 11 points

test_interval: 1 live, priceable Home Depot market at capture time

dataset_version: live DexScreener discovery feed, 24 discovered tokens
execution_assumptions: exit sized against real pool depth via a 2% price-impact budget
hypothesis: A rug/honeypot pre-trade screen combined with depth-capped exit sizing identifies tradeable fresh Solana token launches.
notes: 'The screen working as avoidance rather than selection' -- established that for this asset class, capacity (not selection) is the binding constraint, motivating a8d34f6 and 7aa1ca8.

results.example_volume_vs_liquidity_mismatch: RIKA: $1.3M/day volume against a pool absorbing only $173 on exit

dataset_version: GeckoTerminal volume-ranked pools, 96 established tokens (1-6 months old)
execution_assumptions: capacity measured via 2% price-impact exit sizing
hypothesis: Tokens that survive their first month occupy a sweet spot: liquid enough to size an exit, still inefficient enough (thin) to trade.
notes: Directly echoes the same structural finding as 402eb97 (91% of Polymarket markets traded $0): inefficiency is easy to find precisely where nobody trades, which is why it survives unexploited.

results.mechanism: thin + active is not a stable state -- it either attracts liquidity and stops being thin, or activity dies and depth strands
results.that_one_token: SOL, $26M liquidity -- the opposite of thin

dataset_version: pool reserves math (exact) + assumed payoff tail (Monte Carlo, explicitly not fitted to realized returns)

hypothesis: A many-names/small-size portfolio can convert per-name capacity limits into a viable strategy through width rather than depth.
notes: The unmeasured tail parameter this trial depends on is exactly what ed13f2e / d7597cf / 5386072 then tried, and failed, to pin down.

results.conclusion: positive expectancy that loses almost every time and pays only through a tail this repo could not yet measure; execution is not implemented, example prints intended orders only

dataset_version: 616 pools captured live over a 25-minute window, 2026-07-30
execution_assumptions: candle-history resolution rather than a later re-check, specifically to survive delisted failures
hypothesis: The token payoff tail (Hill alpha) that breadth's Monte Carlo assumed can be measured from a live-captured birth cohort.
notes: A negative methodological result about the data, not just the strategy: establishes how to measure a fat-tail parameter without fooling yourself, which the follow-up (d7597cf, 5386072) then builds on.

results.conclusion: this cohort (616 pools, <1hr observed) cannot resolve the parameter breadth depends on; no mean should be quoted when deleting one dust tick moves it 3 orders of magnitude
results.largest_peak_was: one $0.00074-volume tick in a pool with $6.65 lifetime volume
results.own_bug_found: pool_ohlcv returned [] on rate-limit failure, misclassifying 164/300 pools as never-traded and silently deleting a third of the cohort; fixed to return None for a failed fetch
results.verdict_after_adversarial_review: mostly artifact, biased toward flattering the strategy
results.wash_trading_found: 3 clone mints (XAU/SOL), created 18s apart, volumes within 4 significant figures of each other

search_method: single measurement, five independent adversarial checks applied after the first result looked too good
test_interval: single cohort, first-pass measurement then adversarial re-review

dataset_version: same 616-pool cohort, re-resolved at 3.6 days, 610/616 pools fetched
execution_assumptions: hourly candles spanning each pool's whole life
hypothesis: The same 2026-07-30 birth cohort, re-resolved after 3.6 days with hourly candles covering full pool lifetimes, will pin down the tail index and validate breadth's exit-on-take-profit assumption.
notes: This is the trial that actually ends the breadth/meme-coin line of work -- not an inconclusive tail estimate, but a structural finding (no exit liquidity) that makes the tail-index question moot.

results.conclusion: kills breadth independent of the tail-index question: 95.6% of positions have no counterparty to exit into within a day, so a take-profit exit rule cannot run regardless of the alpha estimate
results.prior_reported_survival_pct: 97.3% at 45min, 98.3% at 3.6 days -- both wrong: a token whose market stops producing candles looks 'alive' at its frozen last price forever

dataset_version: simulated price paths (offline), not live-captured order flow
execution_assumptions: mark-out P&L (adverse selection measured, not assumed away); Kalshi quadratic fee paid on both legs
hypothesis: Fee-aware, inventory-skewed two-sided quoting on binary prediction contracts is profitable once adverse selection (markout) is measured rather than assumed away.
notes: Not a profitability trial by itself -- a mechanism/parameter-correctness trial that found and fixed a real sign/scale bug before any capital-facing conclusion could be drawn from this module.

slow drift never fills a maker that re-quotes every tick
